record.original_question: For Landau's function g(n), the maximal order of an element of the symmetric group S_n, compute g(10^6) and g(10^9). This challenge is explicitly resolved in the source: it reports the value of g(10^6), gives the factorization relation for g(10^9), and describes a later algorithm able to compute g(n) up to n = 10^15.

evidence.quote: I asked as a challenge to compute g(10 6 ) and g(10 9 ).
an algorithm able to calculate g(n) up to n = 10 15

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters, and define Landau's function $g(n)$ to be the maximal order of an element of $S_n$; equivalently,
$$g(n) = \max\{\operatorname{lcm}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_k) : k \ge 1,\ \lambda_i \ge 1,\ \lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_k = n\}.$$
Compute explicitly the values $g(10^6)$ and $g(10^9)$ (for instance, by giving the prime factorization of the corresponding optimal least common multiple), and more generally describe an algorithm that computes $g(n)$ for all $n$ up to $10^{15}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Landau's function has been computed for large values: Jean-Pierre Massias, Jean-Louis Nicolas, and Paul Zimmermann developed algorithms in the 1980s–1990s computing $g(n)$ for $n$ up to $10^4$ and beyond, and Marc Deléglise, Nicolas, and Zimmermann (2008/2009) gave an algorithm computing $g(n)$ for $n$ up to $10^{15}$. Thus $g(10^6)$ and $g(10^9)$ have been computed.

status_evidence.title: Landau's function for one million billions — Deléglise, Nicolas, Zimmermann
status_evidence.snippet: We present an algorithm which has allowed us to compute g(n) up to n = 10^15.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithm computing Landau's function up to 10^15 has been published.

status_evidence.title: OEIS A000793 — Landau's function
status_evidence.snippet: Tables and references include computed values of g(n) for large n by Nicolas and Zimmermann.
status_evidence.claim: Values such as g(10^6) and g(10^9) are known and tabulated.
